question: In its 7th report and in the letter to Georgia, the Commission calls on that country to repeal the law on ‘transparency of foreign influence’ as well as the legislative package on ‘family values and protection of minors’. However, the government’s decision to adopt those laws, which reflect the will of the vast majority of the Georgian people, is sovereign, legitimate and democratic.
The laws were designed to bolster democratic accountability, preserve national identity, further social cohesion and improve institutional transparency.

It is worth remembering that Georgia adopted anti-discrimination legislation back in 2014 protecting LGBTQI+ people against any form of discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and that the concepts of transparency and family values are governed in different ways in different Member States, in conformity with their national competences. 1.
What exactly is the relevance of the link established by the Commission between the protection of LGBTQI+ people and arrangements for the short-stay visa-free regime?
In demanding that laws supported by the majority of the Georgian population be repealed, is the Commission not in danger of undermining the credibility of the EU in Georgian society?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2025) Visa-free travel to the EU is a conditional benefit, contingent upon the fulfilment of specific criteria. One of the criteria is upholding and protecting human rights and fundamental freedoms. Every year the Commission issues a report under the Visa Suspension Mechanism to monitor the EU’s visa-free regimes with third countries, including Georgia.

The progress on recommendations is monitored with reference to the previous year’s report and points towards areas that still require improvement. In the seventh Visa Suspension Mechanism Report adopted on 6 December 20241, the Commission called on Georgian authorities to, inter alia, ensure the protection of fundamental rights of all Georgian citizens.

The Commission recommended to repeal legislation that restricts fundamental rights and freedoms, goes against the principle of non-discrimination and contradicts relevant European and international standards. This includes the Law on ‘transparency of foreign influence’ and the legislative package on ‘family values and protection of minors.

’ In its upcoming eighth Visa Suspension Mechanism Report, the Commission will review to what extent these recommendations have been addressed by Georgian authorities and decide on the possible activation of the suspension mechanism.
